hints: Focus on counting free radicals on each side of the equation, that is the quickest way to tell initiation, propagation and termination apart.
Notice step 1 starts with one radical ($\text{CH}_3\bullet$) and finishes with one radical ($\text{Cl}\bullet$), so radicals are neither created from scratch nor removed.
Apply the same radical count to step 2 and ask yourself what name we give to a step where one radical is used up and a new radical is made to keep the chain going.
walkthrough:
**Recall what the three stages mean**

Think of the chain reaction like a story. Initiation starts the story by making radicals from non-radicals. Propagation keeps the story going. Termination ends it.

Rule to remember:
$$\text{initiation: no radical} \rightarrow \text{radicals}$$
$$\text{propagation: radical} \rightarrow \text{radical}$$
$$\text{termination: radical + radical} \rightarrow \text{no radical}$$

**Test step 1**

Look carefully at what goes in and what comes out.
$$\text{CH}_3\bullet + \text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{Cl}\bullet$$
One radical on the left and one radical on the right. A radical is consumed and a new one is produced, so the chain continues. This is classic propagation.

**Test step 2**

Do the same count again.
$$\text{CH}_3\text{Cl} + \text{Cl}\bullet \rightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{Cl}\bullet + \text{HCl}$$
Again, one radical on the left ($\text{Cl}\bullet$) and one radical on the right ($\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}\bullet$). Even though this is further substitution of $\text{CH}_3\text{Cl}$, the radical pattern is still radical to radical. This is also propagation.

**Make the final decision**

Since both steps use up one radical and generate a new radical to carry on the chain, both steps are propagation steps.

options.A: Incorrect. Initiation must make radicals from stable molecules, e.g. $\text{Cl}_2 \rightarrow 2\text{Cl}\bullet$. Step 1 already starts with $\text{CH}_3\bullet$, so it cannot be initiation.
options.B: Incorrect. Step 1 is correctly a propagation step, but step 2 is not termination. Termination joins two radicals to give no radicals, while step 2 has one radical on each side.
options.C: Incorrect. Neither step fits. Step 1 does not create radicals from scratch, and step 2 does not remove radicals, so neither is initiation nor termination.
options.D: Correct. Both steps show the propagation pattern of one radical in and one (different) radical out, which keeps the free-radical chain going.
